topics.title: Accountable plan travel advances
topics.trigger: An employee receives travel money before the itinerary and receipts are complete.
topics.principle: Business connection, substantiation and return of excess are separate requirements. Paying an advance does not establish that the final reimbursement qualifies.
topics.example: A practice sends a clinician to a conference, advances travel funds and later discovers the hotel refunded one night.

topics.title: Owner reimbursement duplicate charges
topics.trigger: A personally paid expense enters both the bank feed and an owner reimbursement request.
topics.principle: A business record should identify one underlying expenditure and its reimbursement separately. Two payment records do not justify recording the same expense twice.
topics.example: A consultant uploads a card receipt, records a reimbursed expense and also imports the card statement into the business books.

topics.title: Mileage log reconstruction
topics.trigger: An owner has vehicle expenses but incomplete contemporaneous trip records.
topics.principle: A calendar can help identify trips but does not automatically establish deductible mileage. Separate supported business travel, commuting and personal use before selecting a reporting method.
topics.example: A home-service owner remembers several jobs but the odometer readings and appointment locations do not yet agree.

topics.title: Mixed meal and entertainment invoices
topics.trigger: One vendor bill combines business dining with an entertainment event.
topics.principle: Separate the items and supporting purpose. The label on a card statement does not establish the treatment of every part of a bundled purchase.
topics.example: A company hosts customers at a sporting venue and receives one invoice covering seats, meals and transportation.

topics.title: Shareholder distribution basis controls
topics.trigger: A profitable S corporation pays distributions while shareholder basis records lag behind the books.
topics.principle: Cash availability and retained earnings do not establish a shareholder's stock basis. A distribution review needs the shareholder-level history and relevant adjustments.
topics.example: Two owners receive equal cash distributions but contributed different amounts and have different prior-year basis histories.

topics.title: Shareholder loan repayment files
topics.trigger: The company repays money described as an owner loan after several years of losses.
topics.principle: Identify the actual debt and any prior basis reductions. A payment described as principal may require analysis beyond a bank transfer memo.
topics.example: An owner advances operating cash, uses debt basis in earlier years and later receives a partial repayment.

topics.title: Owner health insurance payroll handoff
topics.trigger: An owner-managed corporation pays a policy that also covers family members.
topics.principle: The applicable ownership, entity and payroll reporting rules matter. A health-insurance expense account alone does not establish the owner's individual deduction.
topics.example: A dental practice reimburses its owner for a family policy but the payroll provider has not received year-end instructions.

topics.title: Owner compensation role changes
topics.trigger: An owner's duties change as managers take over daily operations.
topics.principle: Review actual services and compensation facts rather than mechanically carrying forward last year's salary. Distribution decisions and compensation analysis serve different purposes.
topics.example: A restaurant owner moves from daily operations to overseeing multiple managers and a new location.

topics.title: Retirement census reconciliation
topics.trigger: A business considers a retirement contribution while employee records differ between payroll and administration.
topics.principle: The plan administrator needs accurate eligibility and compensation facts. A projected owner contribution is not a substitute for employee coverage analysis.
topics.example: A salon adds employees and transfers a stylist between related entities before the administrator prepares the annual census.

topics.title: Owner retirement funding cash calendar
topics.trigger: An owner wants to reserve cash for retirement contributions alongside payroll and tax payments.
topics.principle: Separate the contribution estimate, approved plan amount and actual funding. Applicable limits, deadlines and deductibility require plan and tax review.
topics.example: A consulting owner receives a large late-year client payment but also owes bonuses and estimated taxes.

topics.title: Quarterly estimated tax forecast revisions
topics.trigger: A forecast changes after a major contract, distribution or household income event.
topics.principle: Preserve the assumptions and prior payments behind each revision. A higher bank balance does not by itself measure current taxable income or payment requirements.
topics.example: A software business receives an annual prepayment while the owner also changes W-2 withholding from another job.

topics.title: Customer deposits and owner cash planning
topics.trigger: Customer cash arrives before the business has completed the related work.
topics.principle: Revenue timing and usable cash require separate review. Keep the contract terms and accounting method visible instead of treating every deposit as distributable profit.
topics.example: A contractor receives a project deposit and orders materials while several earlier jobs remain incomplete.

topics.title: Merchant settlement reconciliation
topics.trigger: Processor deposits are net of fees, refunds and reserves.
topics.principle: Reconcile gross activity to the net cash settlement. A bank deposit is not a complete revenue record when the processor offsets other amounts.
topics.example: An online retailer sees a large sales report but lower bank deposits because returns and rolling reserves were withheld.

topics.title: Business equipment purchase cutoffs
topics.trigger: Equipment is purchased, delivered and installed on different dates.
topics.principle: Payment and readiness for intended use are different facts. Identify the asset and applicable tax-year rules before choosing a depreciation treatment.
topics.example: A manufacturer prepays for equipment in December but installation and testing continue into January.

topics.title: Vendor refund and credit controls
topics.trigger: A vendor credits a prior business purchase after the original expense was recorded.
topics.principle: Trace the credit to the original transaction and period. A later refund should not disappear into miscellaneous revenue without a documented accounting decision.
topics.example: A practice receives a credit for defective supplies that were purchased and expensed in an earlier accounting period.

topics.title: Owner-paid startup costs
topics.trigger: An owner pays formation and launch expenses before the operating business opens.
topics.principle: Organize pre-opening costs separately from later operating expenses and asset purchases. Payment by the owner does not settle capitalization or deductibility.
topics.example: An entrepreneur pays legal fees, training expenses and equipment deposits before the first customer contract begins.

topics.title: Intercompany service charge reconciliation
topics.trigger: Related entities share people or services and transfer money without consistent invoices.
topics.principle: Identify actual work, contractual responsibility and the accounting entry in both entities. A payment label does not prove the charge reflects a genuine service.
topics.example: An operating company pays a management entity while payroll and vendor costs are still split between their bank accounts.

topics.title: Entity election implementation tracking
topics.trigger: An adviser recommends an entity election but the owner has not confirmed filing and acceptance.
topics.principle: Distinguish recommendation, signed filing, submission evidence and subsequent reporting. A planning presentation does not implement an election.
topics.example: An owner discusses an S corporation election in a meeting while the payroll provider continues treating the business as a sole proprietorship.

topics.title: Tax notice response coordination
topics.trigger: A business receives a notice affecting payments, returns or payroll reporting.
topics.principle: Identify the notice, period, response instructions and responsible professional before sending a response. Do not assume a balance notice proves the original return was incorrect.
topics.example: A company receives a payroll notice after changing providers and cannot initially match the agency's payment credits.

topics.title: Tax adviser transition evidence
topics.trigger: A new professional begins work while the old preparer holds important records.
topics.principle: Transfer the complete reporting history and unresolved issues. A PDF return alone may omit workpapers, elections, basis schedules and implementation assumptions.
topics.example: An owner changes firms and supplies tax returns but no depreciation detail, shareholder basis rollforward or open-notice register.
